previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and depression was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had elevated lactate and tachycardia, likely due to volume depletion from recent emesis. Imaging showed cirrhosis but no evidence of obstruction, appendicitis, or colitis. A colonoscopy revealed a polyp in the descending colon, which was removed, with no active inflammation. Her symptoms resolved during the stay, and she was discharged home with a diagnosis of resolved gastroenteritis and functional abdominal pain. She was restarted on lactulose, given a short course of pain medication, and instructed to follow up on pending lab results and polyp pathology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ female with a history of HCV/EtOH  
cirrhosis decompensated by HE, varices and ascites, recent 
colitis, and depression who presented to the ED with abdominal 
pain found to have elevated lactate, CK and transaminitis 
concerning for ischemic colitis s/p colonscopy with polypectomy 
and EGD showing small gastric varices with portal gastropathy.

# Abdominal Pain  
Patient presented with abdominal pain in setting of known 
chronic abdominal pain. Differential included ischemic etiology 
given elevated lactate though colonoscopy findings did not 
support this. It was ultimately felt that patient's abdominal 
pain was most likely secondary to mild alcoholic hepatitis. In 
addition CT abdomen did show bowel wall thickening with possible 
colitis. As a result 5 days of cipro and flagyl were given 
empirically during the hospital course. Work up was negative for 
pancreatitis, gallstones, clot in hepatic and portal 
circulation. Stool studies including c. diff were also negative. 


EGD showed portal gastropathy and small gastric varices with 
repeat EGD recommended in ___ year. Given patient is child's class 
B with small gastric varices nadolol was not felt to be 
indicated. Colonosopy was normal with exception of polypectomy 
with biopsy results pending at time of discharge. CMV viral load 
also checked and pending at time of discharge though felt to be 
unlikely cause of patient's symptoms. Abdominal pain nausea and 
vomitting all improved prior to discharge. It was thought that 
in the future should patient have ongoing abdominal pain with 
elevated lactate that CTA could be completed for further 
evaluation of ischemic etiology. 

#Transaminitis/ elevated CK
AST noted to be elevated greater than ALT likely secondary to 
some degree of alcoholic hepatitis. In addition elevated CK was 
also noted to likely contribute to disproportionately elevated 
AST > 500 initially. Troponins were negative and therefore 
myocardial ischemia was not felt to be a component of elevated 
AST. In addition elevated CK felt to be secondary to electrolyte 
derangements and possible unwitnessed alcohol withdrawal 
seizure. Urine cocaine tox screen also negative. Other 
etiologies for trasaminitis and elevated CK evaluated including 
adenovirus and EBV though these studies were negative. During 
work up of trasaminitis patient noted to not be immune to Hep B 
and vaccination should be considered at time of follow up. CMV 
viral load pending at time of discharge.

# Lactate Elevation  
Patient's elevated lactate in setting of abdominal pain was 
concerning for ischemic colitis vs. poor PO intake in the 
settinig of vomitting as well as decreased metabolism secondary 
to cirrhosis. In addition lactate may have also been elevated 
secondary to unwitnessed alcohol withdrawal seizure. Lactate 
improved with fluid rescussitation. 

# ETOH/HCV crrhosis  
C/b ascites, encephalopathy (multiple admissions last year for 
confusion), 2 grade 1 varices on EGD ___ and portal 
hypertensive gastropathy. HCV genotype 1.  The patient did not 
have evidence of encephalopthy this admission. EGD completed 
that did not show small varices and portal gastropathy. Given 
patient was childs class B with small varices nadolol was not 
felt to be indicated. Spironolactone initially held due to 
dehydration but restarted prior to discharge. Lactulose and 
rifaxaminim were also continued. 

# Hypertension: 
Patient noted to be hypertensive at time of admission secondary 
to pain and this improved with better pain control.

# Sinus tachycardia: 
Noted at time of admission to 100-105 in setting of pain and 
dehydration and improved with pain control and fluid 
rescussitation. 

# Alcohol Abuse  
Initially reported her last drink being ___ weeks prior to 
admission though noted to score on CIWA scale in initially from 
___ requiring ativan. She later told primary team her last 
drink was 2 days prior to admission. It was felt that patient 
had unwitnessed withdrawal seizure from alcohol. CIWA was 
stopped 24 hours prior to discharge. Mulitivtaimn, folic acid, 
and thiamine continued. Patient was also hypomagnesemic, 
hypokalemic, and hypophosphotemic requiring repletion with 
improvement of all metabolic derangements prior to discharge. 
  
# Depression/psychosis  
Followed by psychiatry at ___. Continued home sertraline, 
Seroquel, trazodone, and pramipexole  

# GERD  
- Continued omeprazole

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  Acute onset emesis and right upper quadrant abdominal pain in a
patient with cirrhosis. Evaluate portal vein patency.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The liver is coarsened and nodular in echotexture.The contour of the
liver is nodular, consistent with cirrhosis. There is no focal liver mass.
Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 3 mm
proximally, and 1 cm more distally. This is unchanged compared to ___.

GALLBLADDER: The patient is status post cholecystectomy.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 11.1 cm.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the bilateral kidneys demonstrate no
hydronephrosis, focal mass, or stone.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Patent portal vein in a cirrhotic liver.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with HCV/alcoholic cirrhosis nausea and
vomitting with RUQ and umbilical tenderness on exam with elevated lactate. 
RUQ US unremarkable. Patientw with history of colitis.  // Evaluate for
intrabdominal process

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous contrast administration with split bolus technique.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to PACS for
review.
Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: 741.5 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:



LOWER CHEST:

Atelectasis is noted in the bilateral lung bases. There is no pleural or
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

GENERAL: There is no intra-abdominal free air or free fluid.

HEPATOBILIARY:  The liver is diffusely nodular in contour, compatible with
known cirrhosis.  A subcentimeter hypodensity in the left hepatic lobe is too
small to characterize.  Note is made of recanalization of the umbilical vein. 
The gallbladder is within normal limits, without stones or gallbladder wall
thickening.
PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.
SPLEEN:  The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.
ADRENALS:  The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.
URINARY: Multiple subcentimeter hypodensities are again noted in the right
kidney, too small to characterize, but likely cysts. Otherwise, the kidneys
are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram.  There is no evidence
of stones, solid renal lesions or hydronephrosis. There are no urothelial
lesions in the kidneys or ureters. There is no perinephric abnormality.
GASTROINTESTINAL:  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness and enhancement throughout.  Circumferential wall thickening is
noted in the cecum (02:50), extending to the level of the ascending and
transverse colon. The appendix is normal in appearance.
RETROPERITONEUM:  There is no evidence of retroperitoneal and mesenteric
lymphadenopathy.
VASCULAR:  There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is moderate calcium
burden in the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS:

The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no evidence
of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.



BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is no evidence of worrisome lesions. Abdominal and pelvic wall is within
normal limits.

IMPRESSION:



1. Circumferential cecal wall thickening, extending along the ascending and
transverse colon, is likely due to underlying portal colopathy given known
cirrhosis and portal hypertension. Underlying infectious or inflammatory
colitis cannot be completely excluded.
2. Hepatic cirrhosis.
